metadata.title: ICCS 2022 USER GUIDE FOR THE INTERNATIONAL DATABASE

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This ICCS 2022 user guide documents how variables in the International Database are constructed and scaled for secondary analysis, including indices and scales derived from questionnaire items and a student civic knowledge test. For scales based on IRT, the guide specifies that some scales use IRT WLE scores with a mean of 50 and standard deviation of 10 across equally weighted participating countries that met sample participation requirements; the student civic knowledge test uses IRT plausible values (PV1CIV–PV5CIV) with mean 500 and SD 100 across equally weighted countries. The guide does not provide a single explicit student weight variable name (e.g., W_FSTUWT) or replicate-weight scheme (e.g., BRR/jackknife) for the user’s analysis, so analysts should rely on the ICCS technical documentation for the correct complex-sample weighting variables in the released datasets. Because this document is a user guide rather than an empirical ML study, it does not report whether weights were applied in any model-fitting; instead it instructs how to interpret and use the derived variables and PVs in secondary analyses.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This document is a user guide describing questionnaire instruments, derived variables, and scaling procedures for ICCS 2022, not an empirical analysis predicting outcomes from student-level data. As such, it does not specify an analysis-level missing-data strategy (e.g., listwise deletion or multiple imputation) because no model is estimated here. Missing-data handling is therefore not reported in the context of an ML/empirical results pipeline.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: This is a user guide for the ICCS 2022 International Database and does not define an analytic student sample for an empirical study. It documents that some derived scales are computed using IRT WLE scores across equally weighted participating countries that met sample participation requirements, and it provides PVs for the student civic knowledge test (PV1CIV–PV5CIV). For secondary analyses, the guide implies that analysts should use the released ICCS 2022 datasets and apply the standard ICCS sample participation requirements as described in the ICCS technical documentation, but it does not specify additional inclusion/exclusion filters for a particular analytic model.

data.outcome_summary: This ICCS 2022 user guide explains how to use the ICCS 2022 International Database, including the structure of the National Contexts Survey, School and Teacher questionnaires, and the International Student Questionnaire, as well as how derived indices/scales are constructed. It documents that the student civic knowledge test is scaled using IRT plausible values (PV1CIV–PV5CIV) with mean 500 and SD 100 across equally weighted countries, and that many questionnaire-based scales are reported as IRT WLE scores with mean 50 and SD 10 across equally weighted participating countries that met sample participation requirements. The guide also provides variable naming conventions, national adaptations, and how to interpret derived variables and PV-based outcomes for secondary analysis. Because it is not an empirical research paper, it does not estimate predictive models or report performance metrics; instead, it supports correct downstream analysis of ICCS 2022 variables for policy-relevant research on civic and citizenship education.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This document is a methodological user guide rather than an empirical study with an analytic sample, model estimation, or reported predictive performance. Consequently, fields such as total_students, per-country n_students, ML techniques, and main_findings are not applicable because no target variable is predicted and no model is evaluated. The guide does, however, provide the scaling and variable-construction procedures (including PVs and IRT WLE scales) that are essential for interpreting ICCS 2022 results in subsequent empirical work.
